tool_input.title: shop/api CrashLoopBackOff — bad dnsConfig search domain in rollout
tool_input.content:
On cluster `kind-aurora-lab` (on-prem, cluster_id kubeconfig-6691049da13add50), namespace `shop`, the `api` Deployment went into CrashLoopBackOff immediately after a rollout (revision 2).

**Root cause:** The new revision's pod template set `dnsPolicy: None` with an explicit `dnsConfig.searches` list using suffix `cluster.internal` (e.g. `shop.svc.cluster.internal`, `svc.cluster.internal`, `cluster.internal`). The cluster's actual CoreDNS zone is `cluster.local` (confirmed via `kubectl get configmap coredns -n kube-system -o yaml` → `kubernetes cluster.local ...`). Because of the mismatch, the app's short-name DNS lookup for `redis` (set via `REDIS_HOST=redis` env var) never resolved — logs showed `[Errno -2] Name does not resolve` x5 then `giving up: redis unavailable`, causing the container to exit 1 and crash-loop. Readiness/liveness probes on :8080 then failed because the app never started its HTTP server.

The previous ReplicaSet revision (plain `dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst`, no custom dnsConfig) remained healthy throughout — proving redis itself and the app code were fine; only the new revision's DNS config was broken.

**Why:** Someone/something introduced a custom `dnsConfig`/`dnsPolicy: None` on the `api` deployment template, likely intended to pin a custom DNS search path, but used the wrong cluster domain suffix.

**How to apply next time:**
1. Check `kubectl get pods -n shop` for Error/CrashLoopBackOff + restart count, then `kubectl logs <pod> -n shop --previous` for the real exit reason — don't assume OOM or app bug.
2. Compare the crashing ReplicaSet's pod template against the previous (still-running) ReplicaSet's template — `kubectl get replicaset -n shop -o yaml` — diff dnsPolicy/dnsConfig/env/image.
3. Confirm the cluster's real DNS domain via `kubectl get configmap coredns -n kube-system -o yaml` (look for `kubernetes <domain> ...` in the Corefile) before trusting any custom dnsConfig.
4. Fix: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/api -n shop` (if a healthy earlier revision exists) or edit the deployment to remove the bad dnsConfig / use the correct domain suffix.
